blocks.title: Critical thinking
blocks.text: Critical thinking means questioning information, considering different perspectives and making informed decisions.
When you read about a new technology, look at several sources and viewpoints before forming an opinion.

blocks.prompt: Explain how critical thinking supports responsible use of information, with real-life examples (long question 3).
blocks.explanation: Critical thinking makes us ask who says something, what evidence supports it and what others say before we believe or share it. Examples: a viral message claims a home remedy cures a disease, so we check health authorities and doctors before forwarding it; a product review site praises one brand only, so we compare independent reviews; a news story has a shocking headline, so we read the full article and check other outlets. This prevents spreading misinformation and leads to better decisions.

items: Critical thinking: question, compare viewpoints, then decide.
